subject: pathology
title: Oral cavity and salivary glands: lesions and tumours

steps.tx: Oral white patches demand respect: **leukoplakia** is a clinical white patch that cannot be scraped off or characterised as another disease, carrying dysplasia and malignant risk especially non homogeneous speckled types, while lichen planus gives bilateral lacy Wickham striae and candidiasis wipes off. Erythroplakia (red velvet patch) harbours severe dysplasia far more often than white lesions.
steps.say: White patches that stay may dysplasiate; red velvet patches are worse. Lichen planus laces bilaterally; thrush wipes away. Biopsy non resolving patches.

steps.tx: **Oral squamous carcinoma** follows tobacco, alcohol synergy and betel quid, plus HPV for oropharynx, presenting as non healing ulcers, indurated masses or red white patches with neck node spread. Floor of mouth and lateral tongue are high risk sites. Field cancerisation explains second primaries across the aerodigestive tract after years of exposure.
steps.say: Tobacco, alcohol, betel and HPV grow oral cancers as ulcers that never heal. Tongue edges and mouth floors risk most. Whole tract fields second cancers.

steps.tx: **Pleomorphic adenoma** is the commonest salivary tumour, usually parotid tail, a slow painless biphasic mass mixing epithelial ducts with chondromyxoid stroma like cartilage. Excision must avoid rupture and facial nerve injury because spilled tumour seeds multifocal recurrence, and long standing lesions may transform into carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma.
steps.say: Pleomorphic adenoma mixes ducts with cartilage like stroma in parotids. Slow and painless but rupture seeds recurrences. Old ones may turn malignant.

Benign, cystic oncocytic with lymphoid stroma, may be bilateral
Commonest malignant salivary tumour, graded by cystic and cellular mix
Perineural invasion, late lung metastases, slow but relentless

steps.tx: Malignant salivary clues are pain, rapid growth, facial nerve palsy (parotid) and fixation, contrasting benign slow mobile painless masses. **Mucoepidermoid carcinoma** mixes mucus, intermediate and squamoid cells as commonest malignancy, while adenoid cystic carcinoma creeps along nerves (perineural invasion) with cribriform swiss cheese histology and metastasises late to lungs yet rarely to nodes.
steps.say: Pain, speed, fixation or facial palsy malign salivary lumps. Adenoid cystic creeps nerves to late lung deposits. Mucoepidermoid mixes three cell types commonly.

steps.tx: Sjogren autoimmune sialadenitis destroys glands (covered in autoimmunity) but also predisposes parotid **MALT lymphoma**, so persistent hard parotid enlargement in Sjogren patients needs biopsy rather than reassurance. Mumps virally inflames parotids bilaterally with orchitis risk, while bacterial sialadenitis suppurates in dehydrated elderly with duct stones (sialolithiasis) causing mealtime pain and swelling.
steps.say: Sjogren parotids that harden persistently need lymphoma exclusion. Stones block ducts causing mealtime swelling; mumps swells both parotids virally.
